recipes.name: Grilled Shrimp Scampi
ingredients_raw: 0.25 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes to taste
1.5 pounds medium shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: In a large, non-reactive bowl, stir together the olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, garlic, and black pepper. Season with crushed red pepper, if desired. Add shrimp, and toss to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Preheat grill for high heat. Thread shrimp onto skewers, piercing once near the tail and once near the head. Discard any remaining marinade.
Lightly oil grill grate. Grill for 2 to 3 minutes per side, or until opaque.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Shrimp Scampi
raw_recipe.description: Shrimp marinated in lemon, garlic, and parsley for 30 minutes, then grilled. Can be used as an appetizer or main dish. This recipe also works well for scallops.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you a quick and easy way to cook shrimp. First, the shrimp is marinated in olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, and garlic. Then, it's skewered and grilled for just a few minutes on each side. Try this method with scallops or even chicken tenders. Enjoy the grilled shrimp over cooked rice or angel hair pasta.

review.reviewBody: These were tasty. My husband really liked them. I do have a suggestion if anyone would like to try it and that's add half oil and half butter and about 1/4 cup parm cheese. Place marinade in blender then marinate. The butter mixture will cling to the shrimp and give it more flavor while its cooking.

Since there was only the two of us, hubby just stuck these under the broiler. Delicately seasoned, light, fresh and flavorful. So refreshing to find a shrimp dish not heavily sauced or seasoned. Perfect.

I make this for every bbq at my house and it's always a big hit! I make it in 4lb batches (Costco 4lb bag) and make it w/1 C lemon and a whole head of parsley. It can be made a day ahead less the lemon. Add the lemon 1/2 hr before cooking as instructed. Great recipe! Thanks Holly!

Easy and delicious- make sure you have a hot grill, used colossal shrimp and doubled the marinade ingredients - I also let them marinate for an hour. 2-3 min on each side will give you a little char but perfect shrimp.

The marindate was excellent but I didn't grill the shrimp, I made the traditional scampi dish with angel hair pasta. I used cooked frozen shrimp that were almost thawed and kept them in the marindate for about an hour in the fridge. To make a sauce, I melted a stick of butter, with some pepper, dried parsley, minced garlic (about 5 large cloves), chopped shallots (3) , 1/2 cup chardonnay, squeezed 1.5 lemon juice and added a touch of saffron. I added the shrimp to the sauce until the shrimp were hot (about 5 minutes - careful not to overheat). I also tossed in some steamed broccoli & mushrooms that I cooked separately. Delicious!

Exceptional flavor, considering there's no butter which is why I tried them this way. I marinated the shrimp in a ziplock bag, holding off on the lemon juice just before I skewered them and got the grill ready. Don't skimp on the garlic. That's what makes these soooo good. I had a lemon pepper seasoning that I doused them with before they went on the grill. Served on a bed of rice pilaf with peas, these were superb!

Excellent and easy. I broiled shrimp for about 4 minutes and then added to a sauce made from a medium diced fresh tomato, 1/4 C melted butter, 3 T. lemon juice, 2 cloves of fresh grated garlic, 1/4 C. Chardonnay,1/4 tsp. cayenne, 1 T. dried Parsley and a bit of Lemon Zest,sauteed for about 5 minutes and poured over spaghetti noodles. I was out of Angel Hair which might have been a bit lighter. Will definitely make again.
I made this last night. I don’t have a grill, I put it under a broiler. It is delicious and super easy!!

These were tasty, a keeper for sure. 1.5 lbs isn't enough shrimp for 6 people, though. Bumped it up to 2, and added a little salt to the marinade, too. When they came off the grill (we used a flat grill pan instead of skewers) we tossed them in a bowl with a pat of butter

I had 12 oz of shrimp so basically cut ingredients by 1/3. I used a tad more garlic and a bit less red pepper flakes. I also used a combo of oil and butter and added Parmesan as another viewer suggested. I mixed it and blended in my blender but with this little amount, I think I will use my small good processor next time. Great use of parsley from the garden. Thanks! PS. I broiled my shrimp 3 minutes.

The shrimp was good.......but, making a sauce made this a 5 star....so good! Sauce: Saute 1 stick butter, juice of 1 lemon, 1 T miniced garlic, 1/4 cup veg. oil, 1/2 t. red pepper flakes, and a splash of white wine. Add grilled shrimp and top over pasta. EXCELLENT!!!!
I didn't make any changes. But I did marinate for longer .Very tasty. My fiancé suggested doing the shrimp separately next time.
A solid favorite fir taste and ease of preparation.
Great taste, paired with stone ground grits from Bailey's country store.

Great straight from the grill or chilled as an appetizer. I tried both as is and with the suggestion of using 1/2 oil and 1/2 butter with some parm cheese. While they both were good, both my husband and I preferred the one with the parmesan and butter.
This was a solid dish. Easy and simple. Nothing special but certainly very good and especially for how little work it was to prepare.
